name: John Dewey
role: American philosopher, psychologist and educational reformer (1859–1952)
summary: Dewey was a pragmatist who treated democracy as a way of shared living and joint inquiry rather than only a form of government, and distrusted rule by experts or elites. From the 1930s he rejected laissez-faire liberalism and argued for a socialized, planned economy reached by democratic means, supported unions, workers' rights and a welfare state, and opposed both fascism and Soviet communism. He criticized national-sovereignty absolutism, backed the outlawry of war and an international order, and held that policies and institutions should be judged by tested consequences rather than by general doctrines.

alienated-labor.rationale: He described workers who do not know what they make or its meaning, in a money culture that makes materialism the product of a profit-controlled technology.

arbitrator-settles-disputes.rationale: He listed arbitration treaties and international judicial councils as 'well in their way', though he thought the situation needed more radical thinking.

arms-reduction.rationale: He called schemes of international disarmament and peace movements well in their way while saying they do not go far enough.

central-planning.rationale: Dewey held that 'organized social planning' in which industry and finance are socially directed is the only way to realise liberalism's ends, which says planning beats the unplanned market, though not that it must be centralized.

character-from-environment.rationale: Dewey said social psychology asks how different customs and established arrangements form and nurture different minds, and that habits formed in a social medium create the individual.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Dewey said the genuinely active force behind modern change is scientific method and technology, not class struggle, whose spirit and method he called opposed to science.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: He treated Bernhardi's claim that struggle is the essential principle of life as a failure of nationalism and held that depth of human intercourse is the measure of civilization.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: He held that devotion to money-making and a good time are products of a pecuniary money culture, the serious defect of American civilization.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: He valued social legislation adding social services to government as a decided move away from laissez-faire and as training in organized control, and supported a welfare state.

democracy-best.rationale: He wrote that the cure for the ailments of democracy is more democracy and defended popular government as educative in ways other forms are not.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: He said the democratic idea must not be identified with its external political machinery and is more than a form of government.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: He argued that the subjection of women was no matter for women only but damaged whole societies, and that walls between men and women are barriers to free intercourse.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He argued that an international judicial tribunal must in the end rest on giving up the principle of national sovereignty, and supported the Outlawry of War movement.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He held that a society dividing into masters and slaves corrupts both and that democracy means sharing experience across classes on equal terms.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He called it a wonder that a unified state could exist over a large racially diversified population, against the older assumption that a state needs a homogeneous people, and said America is interracial and international in constitution.

experts-over-public.rationale: Dewey wrote that a class of experts is inevitably removed from common interests and that no government by experts without the masses informing them can be anything but an oligarchy.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Dewey called the idea that society is served by the unplanned coincidence of separate economic actions a leftover of early liberalism and said organized social planning is now the sole method for liberalism's aims (Liberalism and Social Action, ch. 3).

nation-first.rationale: He called the breakdown of the philosophy of nationalism and isolated national sovereignty evident in the war and urged forgoing it, since national interests are not exclusively one's own.

national-self-determination.rationale: He described China's struggle for a unified, independent democracy and condemned Japanese control of Shantung and foreign control of Chinese railways and finance.

natural-rulers.rationale: Dewey was anti-elitist: he held that a wise few lose their wisdom once shut off from the needs of the many and become a class with private interests.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He rejected laissez-faire as the means of liberalism and said he could not find satisfaction in the philosophy of Bolshevik Russia, proposing democratic socialized planning instead.

one-party-rule.rationale: He opposed Soviet communism and fascism and held that democracy depends on open discussion and publicity, which rule by one doctrinal party excludes.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Scholarship describes Dewey's democracy as participatory, with ordinary people taking part in shaping the conditions of their lives and democracy beginning in the local community.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Writing from China in 1919 he blamed the subjection of women, in a 'masculine civilization', for backwardness, corruption and weak public spirit, a remark about China and Japan rather than society in general.

patriotic-education.rationale: He warned against letting education serve narrow national aims and said emphasis should go to what binds people across borders, with national sovereignty secondary.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He asked whether Americans would forgo national sovereignty and submit affairs once thought strictly national to an international legislature, implying he favoured it.

positive-liberty.rationale: Dewey argued that liberty must be supported by the structure of economic organization and that effective liberty of thought and action needs a material basis of security, not only removal of constraint.

production-for-use.rationale: He argued that finance-capitalism profits by maintaining relative scarcity amid potential plenty and that technology under private profit is the fundamental defect, so production should serve a secure material basis for all.

property-fundamental.rationale: He criticized the old doctrine that government's main business is securing property and treated property as an institution to be judged by how it works socially, not as an overriding right.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: He held private property may function socially but said the real issue is the conditions under which it legally operates, judged by its social utility and disutilities.

public-ownership.rationale: He urged liberalism to 'socialize the forces of production' and noted that business might one day welcome public ownership of routinized operations such as railways, without setting out a list of industries.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Dewey wrote that there is one sure road to truth, patient cooperative inquiry by observation and experiment, and that the doctrinal method is limited and private while the method of intelligence is open and public.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He wrote that the problem of 'social control of industry' through governmental agencies would become the open centre of political struggle and called for public control of industry and finance.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: He supported social reforms protecting workers' rights to form unions and to strike, the opposite of legal limits on strikes.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Dewey asked to judge institutions such as private property by how they work in definite times and places, and said general doctrines like Proudhon's or Hegel's do not assist inquiry.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: He held that faith in the continued disclosing of truth through cooperative inquiry is more religious than faith in a completed revelation and treated claims of supernatural inspiration of sacred literatures as discredited.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He called for an order in which 'industry and finance are socially directed' for cultural liberation, which supports public steering of investment without naming strategic industries.

state-harmful.rationale: He treated the state as the organization of the public to regulate indirect consequences of associated action, a necessary function to be improved experimentally, not abolished.

strong-leader.rationale: He wrote that the world has suffered more from leaders and authorities than from the masses and that hero worship grows where face-to-face community is lacking.

unions-good.rationale: Dewey argued for strengthening workers' rights including the rights to form and join unions, and led the teachers' union as its president.

war-builds-character.rationale: He examined the Hegelian and Bernhardi doctrine that war is a preacher against selfish egoism and presented it as the philosophy behind German militarism.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Dewey wrote that control of the means of production by a few operates as a standing coercion of the many, a danger to the liberty of everyone else, and that this coercion exceeds the state's.

women-suffrage.rationale: Scholarship records him as a supporter of women's suffrage.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Scholarship records that Dewey argued for extending democratic control into the workplace.

notes: Mature position: the 1927-1935 books (The Public and Its Problems, Individualism Old and New, Liberalism and Social Action); German Philosophy and Politics (1915) and Democracy and Education (1916) are earlier but consistent. Dewey supported US entry into the First World War (SEP) and later regretted the optimism behind it; no statement here rests on that. Positions the SEP states are medium confidence. Themes searched in the local Gutenberg corpus and archive.org texts: economy and property, planning, unions, democracy and experts, the state, force and revolution, war and internationalism, China and Japan, education, character and habit. Little found on guns, policing, immigration, abortion, religion in public life, environment or technology policy. Freedom and Culture (1939), Why I Am Not a Communist (1934) and Dewey's 1923 outlawry of war essays were not available in open full text.
